hints.content:
We want to complete $x^2\blueD{-8}x$ into a perfect square.

To do that, we should add $\left(\dfrac{\blueD{-8}}{2}\right)^2=\goldD{16}$ to it:

$x^2\blueD{-8}x+\goldD{16}=(x-4)^2$

In order to keep the expression equivalent, we add and subtract $\goldD{16}$, not forgetting the expression's constant term, $-2$:

$\begin{align}
f(x)&=x^2-8x-2
\\\\
&=x^2-8x+\goldD{16}-2-\goldD{16}
\\\\
&=(x-4)^2-2-16
\\\\
&=(x-4)^2-18
\end{align}$

In conclusion, after completing the square, the function is written as

$f(x)=(x - 4)^2 - 18$

This is equivalent to

$f(x)=(x+\blueD{-4})^2-18$
